layer1_identification.workType: stack of three round griddle pancakes
layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized low-poly game asset
layer1_identification.note: reference images are themselves stylized low-poly renders, not photographs; the target look is faceted matte clay, not photoreal

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: flat cylinder stack; footprint is a near-circular rounded polygon
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: radial (approximate) per disk; stack symmetry broken by per-disk XZ offset
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: organic form expressed with geometric faceting

measurements_px.front_elevation_disk_width: top 1200, middle 1210, bottom 1155 (all three effectively equal diameter)
measurements_px.topdown_outline_sides: 18-22 sided rounded polygon, radius wobble roughly +/-3%

derivedRatios.widestPointHeight: mid-rim (equator bulge); the top face perimeter is inset from the widest point

meso_per_disk: top face (slightly crowned, inset from widest point)
micro: pore dimple field on top face
edge sag at the top face perimeter

layer4_spatial: <disk-middle, below, disk-top> contact: flush stacked, small XZ offset
<disk-bottom, below, disk-middle> contact: flush stacked, small XZ offset in a different direction
<pore dimples, embedded-in, top face> contact: embed (concave displacement, not added parts)
no floating parts; each disk rests on the one beneath, contact type = overlap/rest

layer5_materials.roughness: 1.0 (fully matte clay); reference shows no specular lobe anywhere
layer5_materials.relief: faceted planar shading; pores read as concave conical pits with polygonal rims
layer5_materials.runtimeNote: consumer runtime force-replaces every material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map+color, so PBR scalars beyond albedo are inert (repo scripts/breads/types.ts section 2)

layer6_color.observedVsSpec: in the reference renders the rim reads LIGHTER than the top face; that is the upper-left key light striking the outward-facing bevel, not albedo. Spec hexes are used as albedo and the harness key light at (-2,6,2) reproduces the same relationship.

layer7_identity_features: three-layer stack with visible per-layer XZ offset (front elevation shows three distinct rim bands)
pore dimple field: roughly 40 pits on the top face, four size classes (crater 7.5% of diameter, medium 5%, small 2%, tiny 1.3%), sparser within the outer 8% margin
concave faceted pits, each a polygonal cone pushed into the surface (never a raised bump)
hand-poured wobbly outline, not a true circle
two-tone crust: lit top face vs deeper rim/underside
edge sag: the top face perimeter droops below the widest point of the rim
layer8_uncertainty: underside of every disk is hidden in all three views (occluded by the disk below / by the ground plane); modelled as a closed low-detail cap and never visible from any turntable azimuth above the horizon
the interior between stacked disks is hidden; contact is modelled as a small overlap rather than a solved crease
exact pore positions are not identity-critical and are procedurally seeded from the builder rng; size distribution and count are matched instead
reference renders carry a soft contact shadow between layers that the flat-lit harness will not reproduce; this is expected, not a defect
